segments.text:
Verſ. 27.
He ſaith to the deepe, Be dry, and I will dry vp thy floods.

SOme thinke the Prophet deſcribes Babylon here vnder a figure; neither doe I denie but it may be heere comprehended: yet I cannot allow that it ſhould be onely reſtrained to her. For I had rather take it for ſome vnexpected mutation; becauſe hee ſhewes there will be a neceſſitie of ſuch a rare chāge, as if the people were to be drawne out of the bottome of the ſea: but he reſolues them, that God will be omniſufficient to ouercome all lets and impediments. As I thinke therefore, Iſaiah rather alludes to that firſt deliuerance, at what time God brought the people out of Egypt through the midſt of the ſea: as if he ſhould ſay; I haue done this for your fathers, hope for the like at my hands now, and thinke not that the waies through which you are to paſſe homeward, ſhall be ſtopped vp againſt you.
